home.name: Raphael Scharf Passos
home.phrase: Back-ends in C# and Python, and process automation.
home.status: Looking for an IT internship: afternoons, on-site or hybrid in Curitiba, or remote.
home.letter:
Hi! Glad you made it to the desk.
I'm Raphael, feet in Curitiba and head in code. I study Software Engineering at Universidade Positivo, and before that I took a technical course in Systems Analysis and Development at SENAI.
What I like most is taking repetitive work and turning it into a system: that is how Fleet Automation came about, reading insurance policies in PDF and handing back a ready spreadsheet. For UniCar I built the whole API of a carpool app, with real-time chat and location.
Before that I looked after the computers and the people at Biobanco, so I know what it is like to help someone in a hurry and actually fix the problem.
Outside code: movies, the PS2, cars, boxing, good music and a good perfume. Most of it is scattered around this penthouse.
I'm looking for an IT internship in the afternoons, on-site or hybrid in Curitiba, or remote. If you liked it, the PDF is right below and the car radio has my contacts.

unicar.name: UniCar
unicar.description: Carpooling app for university students in Curitiba. API with JWT login and college e-mail verification, real-time driver location and chat, routes and pricing with Google Maps, and integration tests.

frotas.name: Fleet Automation
frotas.description: Internal system for an insurance brokerage in Curitiba: it reads fleet policies in PDF from several insurers, extracts the vehicles and generates a standardized Excel file, with pending-item review, history and versions.

about.title: About me
about.aboutText:
I live in Curitiba, study Software Engineering in the mornings and I'm looking for an afternoon internship. I like understanding how an operation works on the inside and building the system that takes the repetitive work out of it, as I did in Fleet Automation, made for a real insurance broker.

Much of what I know I learned on my own, outside the classroom. This portfolio is an example: nobody asked for it, I built it because I wanted to learn 3D and make something different. Almost everything in this room is modeled in code, with React Three Fiber and TypeScript.

I like projects with a beginning, middle and end: understanding the problem, writing the back-end, testing it and shipping something people use every day.

magnolia.notes: A chaotic, dramatic mosaic of lives crossing in Los Angeles in surreal ways. Intense, suffocating and full of broken people begging for a drop of peace.

donnie.notes: A cult classic about a lonely teenager dealing with the silhouette of a giant rabbit in the 80s. It mixes delirium, time travel and a damn melancholic atmosphere that leaves you thinking for days.

arrival.notes: Science fiction that is not about guns or explosions, but about the weight of time and communication. Language is the wildest weapon here, and the ending hits your head hard.
